A first-class, second-class, and third-class lever placed vertically. Top panel: A horizontal bar (First-class lever) with a triangular Fulcrum in the middle. An Effort arrow pushes down on the left end, and a Load weight is on the right end. Middle panel: A horizontal bar (Second-class lever) with a triangular Fulcrum at the far left. A Load weight is in the middle, and an Effort arrow pulls up on the right end. Bottom panel: A horizontal bar (Third-class lever) with a triangular Fulcrum at the far left. An Effort arrow pulls up in the middle, and a Load weight is on the right end. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A simple block and tackle system showing two fixed pulleys in an upper block and two movable pulleys in a lower block. A rope is threaded through them, with one end attached to the bottom of the upper block, winding down to a lower pulley, up to an upper pulley, and so on, terminating in a downward pull arrow labelled 'Effort (E)'. A heavy crate hangs from the lower block, labelled 'Load (L)'. The four vertical rope segments supporting the movable block should be clearly visible. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A simple screw jack. The main threaded screw has threads separated by a distance labelled 'Pitch (p)'. At the top of the screw is a horizontal handle (tommy bar) of length 'r'. A downward arrow at the end of the handle is labelled 'Effort (E)', and a large weight resting on top of the jack is labelled 'Load (L)'. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A wheel and axle machine shown as two concentric cylinders on a common shaft. The large cylinder (Wheel) has radius 'R', with a rope wrapped around it and an arrow pointing down labelled 'Effort (E)'. The small cylinder (Axle) has radius 'r', with a separate rope wrapped in the opposite direction and an attached weight labelled 'Load (L)'. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A right-angled triangular inclined plane. The horizontal base, the vertical height labelled 'h', and the slanted length labelled 'L'. An angle 'θ' is marked between the base and the incline. A square block labelled 'Load (L) = mg' rests on the incline, with an arrow pointing parallel up the slope labelled 'Effort (E)'. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.
